items.title: 中共五中全會開幕：十三年反腐後，如何繼續「從嚴治黨」？
items.desc: 中國政壇至今沒有明確的接班人。受訪專家認為，這反映習近平面臨兩難：不指定接班人有助維持權威，指定接班人則可能提前形成新的權力中心。

items.title: 巴西總統盧拉：北京在美國後院的「老朋友」第四次贏得大選
items.desc: 盧拉總統意外獲勝，但他將面對一個充滿敵意的國會和一個兩極分化的國家。

items.title: 中國市場放緩，英國傳統精英私立學校紛紛進軍印度
items.desc: 多所英國傳統精英私校近年相繼在印度開設分校，瞄準當地日益壯大的富裕階層。隨着中國教育監管收緊，加上英國私校面臨稅務壓力，印度成為新的擴張目標。

items.title: 住着一群代孕孩子，美國加州的豪宅如何變成「恐怖之家」？
items.desc: 美國加州一棟豪宅因男嬰受傷揭發涉嫌虐童案，屋內住着多名透過代孕出生的孩子。涉案男女被控串謀虐待兒童，事件亦引發外界關注美國代孕產業的監管問題。

items.title: 美國中選舉前夕，奧巴馬抨擊特朗普政府
items.desc: 奧巴馬表示，這場選舉是「至少能抑制本屆政府某些愚蠢行徑的最後一次最佳機會」。

items.title: 日本以舉辦世界級活動聞名，但名古屋亞運卻是一片混亂
items.desc: 飯店混亂、交通事故和外交失誤使組織者和承辦的公司成為焦點。

items.title: 法國再爆大規模示威逾1300人被捕，警民衝突致53警受傷
items.desc: 法國當局表示，數十萬民眾周六再次在全國各地參與抗議活動。示威大致和平進行，但部分城市其後爆發警民衝突，全國有超過1,300人被捕，53名警員受傷。

items.title: 巴黎騷亂中的三位華人：「激烈的地方激烈，安靜的地方安靜」
items.desc: 三位受訪者表示，暴力事件集中於示威區域，市民日常生活並未受到太大影響。但他們對政府能否平息抗議並不樂觀，甚至有人預計，隨著冬季來臨、生活成本上漲，示威還會陸續出現。

items.title: 西藏那曲7級地震16死54傷，當局派翼龍無人機進行災情偵察
items.desc: 地震發生在西藏東北部一個山區且人口稀少的地區。

items.title: PHP是什麼？為何它引發全球網絡安全危機？
items.desc: 人工智能發現了長期未被察覺的程式漏洞，引發全球罕見的大規模網絡安全應對行動。

items.title: 特朗普治下，美國經濟的真實表現如何？
items.desc: 中期選舉前夕，特朗普一直吹噓美國經濟的表現。 BBC事實查核（BBC Verify）調查美國的通貨膨脹、就業和經濟成長。

items.title: 暗影人物：與烏克蘭合作的俄羅斯人
items.desc:
從線人和秘密網絡，到破壞行動及暗殺的指控，俄羅斯與烏克蘭之間的戰爭，正越來越多地在遠離戰場的地方展開。
這場暗影戰爭的許多細節難以核實。不過，《BBC之眼》罕有地接觸到一些俄羅斯人。他們聲稱，自己正通過在俄羅斯境內執行行動，以協助烏克蘭。BBC已確認他們為烏克蘭情報機構工作，但未能獨立核實他們所稱參與的行動。

items.title: 《孤獨的美食家》：一個人吃飯，為什麼能紅遍全亞洲？
items.desc: 開播至今14年，《孤獨的美食家》從日本深夜劇成長為風靡亞洲的電視作品。觀眾跟隨主角井之頭五郎穿梭街巷尋找美食和故事。主演松重豐希望讓更多海外觀眾透過美食認識日本文化。

items.title: 美沙冬是毒還是藥？從香港經驗看台灣選戰戒毒爭議
items.desc: 台北市長選舉引發對「美沙冬」（香港稱「美沙酮」）與毒品減害政策的論戰，然而在海峽對岸的香港，這項計劃已運作超過半世紀。為什麼醫學界將其視為有效降低犯罪與血液傳染病的「減害」關鍵？

items.title: 新鴨綠江大橋閒置12年終開通：中朝關係回暖？
items.desc: 連接中國與朝鮮的鴨綠江大橋，在閒置12年之後終於正式開通。近年朝鮮與俄羅斯關係愈走愈近，專家分析中方需要透過開通大橋鞏固對朝關係，也被視為關係回暖的象徵。

items.title: 台灣AV盛極而衰：中國市場如何催生這場成人片熱潮？
items.desc: 台灣曾被視為亞洲唯一能合法拍攝無碼成人影片的地區，並在2020年前後快速擴張。隨著片商「麻豆傳媒」停運，外界開始質疑這波繁榮是否與中國市場及博弈資金有關。

items.title: 普京提議中美俄「三方會談」：特朗普響應，北京未表態，基輔反對
items.desc: 在普京建議三方於APEC期間進行會談後，特朗普表示願意參與，強調會談重點將是無核化問題。目前中方尚未就三方會談表態。

items.title: DeepSeek被美國政府系統禁用：中美AI競爭繼續升溫

items.title: 為何特朗普在國宴上送習近平一座華麗的白頭海鵰雕像？
items.desc: 從紅杉木長椅到DVD，饋贈禮物一直是外交藝術的重要一環。

items.title: 從年輕縣官到國家主席：習近平41年來的訪美影像

items.title: 為甚麼馬斯克要策劃 SpaceX 與特斯拉的超大型合併？

items.desc: In this arts24 music show, Jennifer Ben Brahim brings us a roundup of the big music releases and news of the week, from US rapper Macklemore's charity stadium shows to raise money for Palestine, to the return of R'n'B crooner John Legend with his 11th album "Muse" – his first collaboration with close friend Pharrell Williams.

items.title: France protests: Macron rules out state of emergency
items.desc: The French government sought to draw a line Monday under weeks of protests that have been marred by violence, with President Emmanuel Macron heading to Marseille. France has been rocked by widespread anger over the rising cost of living, with nationwide demonstrations on October 17 degenerating into some of the country's worst rioting in years.

items.title: Lula's re-election brings hope for the Amazon as deforestation drops to record low
items.desc: Climate activists in Brazil and beyond are celebrating President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's election victory as good news for the Amazon rainforest. His last four years in power saw a record decrease in deforestation in the world's largest rainforest, appropriately nicknamed the planet's lungs. FRANCE 24's Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe tells us more.

items.title: Jordan arrests three following deadly terror attack on church
items.desc: Jordanian authorities on Monday arrested three terrorists following a deadly attack on a church during a funeral procession that killed nine people in the western village of Hammoud. The three assailants – who are Islamic extremists, according the Jordanian director of public security – were injured in a dawn shootout with authorities and are due to be brought before the courts in the nation that supports capital punishment.

items.title: Brazil's Lula reelected president in runoff vote: A look back at his career
items.desc: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won an unprecedented fourth term on Sunday (October 25), the country's electoral court said, in a shock result that defied polls.

items.title: US Midterms 2026: A history of gerrymandering
items.desc: What does a salamander have to do with US elections? Dating back centuries, gerrymandering continues to play a role in American elections today. Used more often by Republicans in the modern era of voting, Democrats have also resorted to the tactic in the past decade. But what is gerrymandering, and why is it called that? FRANCE 24's Tanishk Saha explains.

items.title: Macron promises 'concrete measures' in response to French students' demands
items.desc: French President Emmanuel Macron said the government would announce “concrete measures" on Monday (October 26) to address school students’ demands after weeks of unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu was scheduled to meet with students later Monday. FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago reports from the ground.

items.title: US midterms: Obama blasts Trump's 'chaos and cruelty' while campaigning for Democrats
items.desc: Ten days out from the elections that will determine control of the closely divided Congress, Barack Obama took to the campaign trail to accuse the Republican president of corruption, deride his strategy for Iran and skewer the gilded aesthetic he has applied ‌to White House renovations. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson tells us more.

items.title: Tens of thousands of Israelis living abroad expected to fly in for pivotal vote
items.desc: Israelis are preparing to head to the polls on Tuesday (October 27). Unable to vote from abroad, tens of thousands of expatriate citizens have been flying in from across the world to cast their ballots. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky met some of them at the airport.

items.title: Serbia's Vucic concedes defeat to the student-led movement: What's next?
items.desc: Serbia's student-led protest movement won a historic victory in parliamentary ⁠election, ending the ​long rule of Aleksandar Vucic and sparking mass celebrations. But their yet-to-be named leaders face a long list of issues. FRANCE 24's Angela Diffley gives us her analysis.

items.title: Lula wins fourth term: What are the reactions in Brazil?
items.desc: Brazil's leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva was re-elected against all expectations on Sunday (October 25), but his conservative rival Flavio Bolsonaro refused to accept the loss and said he would seek to have the vote annulled. FRANCE 24's Jan Onoszko tells us more.

items.title: Bolsonaro's refusal to concede underscores ‘serious’ challenges to Brazil's democratic institutions
items.desc: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Dr Pedro Perfeito da Silva, Latin American specialist at the University of Exeter. For Dr Perfeito da Silva, Lula's stunning success reflects the convergence of digital organizing, grassroots mobilization, targeted socioeconomic appeals and an effective effort to mobilise opposition to the Bolsonaro political project. As he explains, Lula assembled a coalition that "not only energized his supporters but also attracted voters from groups that had been somewhat skeptical of the government in the first round."

items.title: Will Netanyahu's security promise win him this election?
items.desc: Since the beginning of his political career, Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, has campaigned on a promise that he is the only one who will keep the Jewish state safe. As Israelis head to the polls for their first election since the October7 Hamas attacks and the start of the war in Gaza, Netanyahu's strategy might be less effective. FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler explains.

items.title: Lula wins Brazil election but faces uphill battle to govern
items.desc: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's narrow election victory on Sunday has dealt a blow to Brazil's far right, but deep political divisions remain. The newly re-elected president must tackle economic and security concerns at home while navigating international tensions with US President Donald Trump.

items.title: Belgrade in rapture as Serbian students topple Vucic in historic election
items.desc: Serbia's student-led movement declared victory in parliamentary elections Sunday ending 14 years in power for Aleksandar Vucic's right-wing populist party. Vucic conceded defeat less than two hours after polls closed, triggering raucous scenes in the capital as supporters of the movement celebrated the defeat of a government they blamed for deep-rooted corruption.

items.title: Live: French student representatives hail ‘concrete measures’, call for protests to continue
items.desc: Representatives from French high school student groups on Monday hailed the government’s first measures to calm the crisis over ongoing unrest linked to their protest movement, including a gradual replacement of higher education admissions platform Parcoursup, but called for “continued mobilisation” after their meeting with Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu. Follow our liveblog for all the latest.
